raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
<!-- markdownlint-disable -->

## Overview

Stacked on #62171 (row-length single pass); only the last commit is new.

`cooperative_topk` now also reads BF16 logits. On SM100 the DSA indexer then keeps the paged MQA logits in BF16
instead of upcasting them to FP32 before the decode top-k. This extends what main already does for
`deep_select`.

## Claims

- One fewer kernel per indexer decode call on SM100/SM103 (the FP32 upcast `as_fp32_logits`), and the top-k reads
  half the bytes.
- The selected top-k values are the same as from the FP32 upcast: BF16 widens to FP32 exactly. Among exactly
  equal logits, which index wins was already unspecified.
- DCP, top-k backends that take only FP32, and BF16 rows that are not 16-byte aligned still upcast as before.
- On InferenceX AgentX, GLM-5.3 vs SGLang: together with #62170 and #62171, decode time on the same turns drops 2.0-2.9% on 4x GB200 (2.5-4.1% on 4x B300) at concurrency 1-16; by the forward benchmark this PR is about 1/3 of that.

## Validation

- `tests/kernels/test_top_k_per_row.py` on B300 (SM103): 285 passed, 37 skipped.
  - `test_cooperative_topk_rows_shorter_than_stride` now runs FP32 and BF16 logits through every cluster size and
    both paths. It compares the selected values with `torch.topk` and checks that no index repeats.
  - `test_sparse_indexer_topk_backend_resolution` checks when BF16 logits skip the upcast: `auto` or `cooperative`
    within the row limit, with a 16-byte-aligned stride. `persistent` and over-limit batches still upcast.
- Kernel time on B300 is the same for BF16 and FP32 input (10.3 us at 4 rows x 40K, 11.1 us at 16 rows), so the
  saving is the upcast kernel and its extra pass over the logits.
- Target verify forward latency (`vllm bench forward`, GLM-5.2-NVFP4, TP4, dummy weights, exact KV lengths, MTP verify shapes of B requests x 4 tokens, `max_model_len` 1M, CUDA graph; spread < 0.1%), B300, on top of #62170 and #62171:

  | shape | before (us) | after (us) |
  |---|---|---|
  | 1x4 @25K | 8630.6 | 8589.8 (-0.47%) |
  | 3x4 @25K | 12136.9 | 12090.4 (-0.38%) |
  | 7x4 @25K | 17547.7 | 17497.8 (-0.28%) |
  | 1x4 @94K | 8702.3 | 8654.3 (-0.55%) |
  | 3x4 @94K | 12361.1 | 12284.4 (-0.62%) |
  | 7x4 @94K | 17940.9 | 17806.9 (-0.75%) |

  In an nsys node-level trace of the batch-1 verify graph, `_upcast_logits_kernel` (36 us per step) is gone.

- Exactness: with real MTP verification (32 GSM8K questions, greedy, one at a time), this PR stacked with the other GLM-5 top-k changes gives the same outputs (32/32) and the same acceptance length (3.4904) as main.
- End to end on B300 x4 (SM103): GLM-5.2-NVFP4, TP4, MTP 3 with synthetic acceptance length 3.0 (fixed step count), `max_model_len` 1M, FP8 KV, CUDA graphs (default sizes). Decode ms/token per request, median of 9 repetitions of (T1200 - T200) / 1000 on cached prompts (repetition spread at B=1 is about 1.5%), on top of #62170 and #62171:

  | context | B | before | this PR |
  |---|---|---|---|
  | 25K | 1 | 3.145 | 3.132 (-0.4%) |
  | 94K | 1 | 3.190 | 3.167 (-0.7%) |
  | 94K | 7 | 5.814 | 5.740 (-1.3%) |

<details>
<summary>InferenceX AgentX setup and full results (GLM-5.3-NVFP4, vLLM vs SGLang)</summary>

InferenceX c801c9f2d AgentX scenario (pinned AIPerf), 20-minute fast mode, GLM-5.3-NVFP4 rev e3b8f9f2, TP4, MTP 3
(synthetic acceptance 2.99), native KV offload 135 GB per rank, Rust frontend, MoE autotune, `max-num-seqs` =
2 x concurrency. vLLM is main dcd07967ca with its default linear backend and default CUDA graph config, plus the
PRs cumulatively. SGLang a916d91cd3 with IMEX, TRT-LLM all-reduce fusion, `--mem-fraction-static 0.90`. Fresh
server per point, SGLang and the four vLLM variants alternating per concurrency. "Decode" is request latency minus
TTFT, summed over the turns both runs finished (a few hundred per point); fast-mode throughput alone moves about
+-2% between runs.

4x GB200 (c=1/4 on driver 580.173.02; c=8/16 on 580.178.04 after a host reinstall, SGLang rerun there too):

| decode time vs SGLang, same turns | main | + #62170, #62171, #62172 | + #62174 (flashinfer-ai/flashinfer#6630, flashinfer-ai/flashinfer#6631, flashinfer-ai/flashinfer#6632) | + #62173 |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| c=1 | +8.9% | +5.8% | +4.0% | +3.2% |
| c=4 | +12.7% | +10.6% | +7.3% | +7.3% |
| c=8 | +12.3% | +9.5% | +7.9% | +7.3% |
| c=16 | -22.6% | -25.0% | -24.5% | -24.3% |

| tok/s/GPU vs SGLang | main | + #62170, #62171, #62172 | + #62174 | + #62173 |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| c=1 (SGLang 5,681) | -3.2% | -0.4% | -1.1% | +0.6% |
| c=4 (SGLang 6,783) | -0.6% | -2.4% | +0.4% | -1.7% |
| c=8 (SGLang 11,799) | -11.5% | -9.4% | -8.8% | -8.4% |
| c=16 (SGLang 10,529) | +44.7% | +45.6% | +45.8% | +46.8% |

| decode time vs the previous column, same turns | + #62170, #62171, #62172 | + #62174 | + #62173 |
|---|---|---|---|
| GB200 c=1 / c=4 / c=8 / c=16 | -2.9% / -2.0% / -2.1% / -2.9% | -1.6% / -3.1% / -1.2% / -0.4% | -0.8% / -0.9% / -0.5% / -0.1% |
| B300 c=1 / c=4 | -2.5% / -4.1% | -1.6% / -3.1% | -0.5% / -1.1% |

#62170, #62171 and #62172 were measured together; `vllm bench forward` (target verify forward, spread < 0.1%)
splits their gain about 1/6, 1/2 and 1/3.

</details>

## Details

- `CooperativeTopKParams`, the TMA staging buffers and the histogram loads are templated on the input type.
- TMA units are 16 bytes (8 BF16 or 4 FP32 elements), so the stride and per-block alignment follow the element
  size.
- Scores are widened to FP32 when binned, so both input types use the same radix keys.
- The extension dispatches on `logits.scalar_type()`.
- `SparseIndexerTopk.takes_bf16_logits` reports whether the resolved backend reads BF16 directly: `cooperative`
  (also as `auto`'s choice) when its constraints hold, and `deep_select`. The indexer upcasts only when it doesn't
  or when DCP is on. This replaces main's `topk_backend != "deep_select"` check with the same rule extended to
  `cooperative`.
- Candidate-block selection (DeepSeek-V4.1) already handles BF16 logits under `deep_select`. With `cooperative` it
  now gets them too. I could not run that model here.

---

<details>
<summary> Pull Request Checklist </summary>

- [x] I used vLLM's `/pr-checklist` skill. (Mandatory for agents, optional for humans).
- [x] AI assistance was used during the creation of this PR.

- [x] **Design Fit:** Minimizes impact on core components, reuses existing functionality, and justifies added complexity.
- [x] **Testing and Validation:** Validates the change and ensures any added tests are meaningful and reliable, with CI coverage or documented CI resource constraints and validation performed outside CI.
- [x] **Code Quality and Style:** Keeps code and comments clear and concise, and updates relevant documentation and examples.
- [x] **Pull Request Contents:** Includes a brief summary and relevant links, supports claims with evidence, explains root causes and implementation trade-offs, and follows the contributing guide.
</details>

@@ -1361,6 +1361,46 @@ def test_deepseek_topk_backends_no_error_and_reference(
     )
 
 
+@pytest.mark.skipif(not _has_device_capability(90), reason="This test requires SM90+")
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("top_k", [512, 2048])
+# 1-4 rows take the 16-CTA cluster on SM100 (8-CTA below), then 8, 4 and 2.
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("num_rows", [1, 4, 8, 33, 64])
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("stride", [65536, 1048576])
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("dtype", [torch.float32, torch.bfloat16])
+@torch.inference_mode()
+def test_cooperative_topk_rows_shorter_than_stride(
+    top_k: int, num_rows: int, stride: int, dtype: torch.dtype
+) -> None:
+    """Each row picks its single-pass or streaming path from its own length,
+    so one launch over a wide logits buffer mixes both. BF16 logits are read
+    as-is."""
+    torch.set_default_device("cuda:0")
+    set_random_seed(0)
+    # Trivial (<= top_k), register (<= 16384) and cluster paths, the longest
+    # rows streaming through two passes on small clusters.
+    row_lengths = [min(stride, 300000), 40000, 16384, 5000, 300]
+    lengths = [row_lengths[i % len(row_lengths)] for i in range(num_rows)]
+    logits = torch.randn(num_rows, stride).to(dtype)
+    workspace = torch.empty(RADIX_TOPK_WORKSPACE_SIZE, dtype=torch.uint8)
+    out = torch.empty(num_rows, top_k, dtype=torch.int32)
+    torch.ops._C.cooperative_topk(
+        logits, torch.tensor(lengths, dtype=torch.int32), out, workspace, top_k, stride
+    )
+    for row, length in enumerate(lengths):
+        k = min(top_k, length)
+        idx = out[row]
+        assert torch.all(idx[k:] == -1)
+        # BF16 logits carry exact ties, among which any index may win, so
+        # compare the selected values.
+        assert idx[:k].unique().numel() == k
+        torch.testing.assert_close(
+            logits[row, idx[:k].long()].sort().values,
+            logits[row, :length].topk(k).values.sort().values,
+            atol=0,
+            rtol=0,
+        )
+
+
 @pytest.mark.skipif(not _has_device_capability(90), reason="This test requires SM90+")
